notes.note: Set B correctly extracts total thickness values that align with the chart's y-axis grid lines (e.g., 45mm at 15%, 40mm at 25%). Set A frequently assigns these total stack heights to specific thin layers like 'glass_biax' or 'CarbonUD' (e.g., claiming glass_biax is 42mm), which contradicts the visual legend where those layers are thin strips on top of the main foam block.

Set A correctly interprets the stacked bar chart, identifying the total web thickness and reasonably estimating the thick foam layer versus the thin glass_biax layer. Set B fundamentally misreads the chart legend, attributing the total bar height (primarily foam) to 'glass_biax thickness' or 'CarbonUD thickness', resulting in physically impossible values (e.g., 42mm glass_biax when the total is 40mm). Set A has minor reading inaccuracies on the smallest bars, but Set B's errors are pervasive misbindings of values to the wrong material properties.

Set B's numbers are consistent with the stacked bars in Figure 2-9: total shear-layup thicknesses of about 45/40/35/30/25/20/15/10 mm across the span positions, plus plausible small glass_biax (~3 mm) and dominant medium_density_foam splits. Set A repeatedly binds total stack heights to glass_biax (42 mm at 25%, 45 mm at 15%, 32 mm at 44%, 12 mm at 100%, 38 mm at 33%) and foam-scale values to CarbonUD (23 mm at 54%, 13 mm at 77%), even though the carbon plies are only a thin bottom sliver. Set A also contradicts itself (glass_biax 1 vs 3 mm at 77%, 3 vs 4 mm at 64%) and adds trivial zero-Thickness CarbonUD claims for the empty circular 0%/2% positions. Set B's weakness is that its 'thickness' claims omit the layer (vague total-stack thickness) and it drops web0 at 64%, but nothing in it is clearly misbound.

Set A correctly reads the stacked-bar totals (45/40/35/30/25/20/15/10 mm across the span positions) and gives plausible per-layer values for glass_biax and medium_density_foam, keeping web0/web1 and span position as conditions. Set B repeatedly binds the total stack height to a single thin layer (glass_biax 45/42/38/32/12 mm, CarbonUD 13/23 mm), which is plainly wrong given the 0–60 mm axis and the layer legend, and it also contradicts itself (glass_biax 42 mm vs 4 mm at FFA-W3-360 25% for both webs; 12 mm vs 3 mm at FFA-W3-211 100%). B additionally emits trivial zero-thickness claims for the empty circular 0%/2% positions and its quotes are bare token lists that do not support any numeric value. A is clearly the more faithful set despite a few uncertain layer readings.

remarks.remark: Layer-segment values can only be estimated from the bar chart (no data labels), so fine splits (glass_biax 3 vs 4 mm, foam 25 vs 27 mm) are hard to verify; I penalized only claims that are impossible against the bar totals. The web0 and web1 panels look nearly identical, yet both sets give different web0/web1 values at the same span position (e.g. B: foam 13 vs 10 mm at 77%, 27 vs 25 mm at 44%) — worth checking against the source data. Both sets omit gelcoat, glass_triax and glass_uni layer thicknesses entirely.

Both sets build quotes by stitching non-contiguous text-layer fragments ('...'), so no quote is a literal passage; B's quotes ('web0, FFA-W3-360 25%, glass_biax') never contain the axis or any number and cannot support the values. The web0 and web1 panels look nearly identical, yet A gives different medium_density_foam values for the two webs at the same span position (13 vs 10 mm at 77%, 27 vs 25 mm at 44%) — at least one of each pair is likely a misread, but the bars are too small to resolve. Neither set extracts the thin layers (CarbonUD, Gelcoat, glass_triax, glass_uni) or states that the circular 0%/2% positions have no web/layup, and neither records the figure caption as context for the 'thickness' attribute, which A leaves otherwise unnamed.
